Framing and exact resolver: this targets BLS CES series CES0500000003, average hourly earnings of all employees on private nonfarm payrolls, total private, seasonally adjusted, for the June 2026 Employment Situation first print. The run timestamp is after the scheduled release, so the forecast evidence is restricted to public information available before the June first print.

reasoning.text: Variant consistency: all anchors are total private average hourly earnings for all employees, seasonally adjusted, CES0500000003/Table B-3. I did not mix in not-seasonally-adjusted CEU0500000003 or production-and-nonsupervisory earnings.

Prior/update/interval: base rate / reference class prior is persistence around recent CES0500000003 monthly percent growth before the June print. From fetched pre-release levels, recent changes are Jan-Feb 100*(37.27/37.15-1)=0.323, Feb-Mar 100*(37.35/37.27-1)=0.215, Mar-Apr 100*(37.41/37.35-1)=0.161, and Apr-May first print 100*(37.53/37.41-1)=0.321. The sample standard deviation of these percent changes is sigma = 0.080 percentage point, so the 80 percent half-width is about 1.28*sigma = 0.102 percentage point. Centering on a persistence prior of 0.28 gives bounds 0.28 +/- 0.10 = 0.18 to 0.38.

Level, momentum, one-off, and mechanism effects: wage growth had been steady near 0.3 percent, but the pre-release sample also contained softer 0.16 to 0.22 percent months. With no pre-release evidence of a June wage shock, persistence plus modest mean reversion is the main adjustment.

Counter-consideration: upside risk would be a high-wage sector mix jump or broad wage acceleration that would land above the interval, while downside risk would be a sharper low-wage-to-high-wage composition reversal or weak hiring mix that would land below the interval. An outside the interval outcome would be below 0.18 percent or above 0.38 percent on the first-print MoM measure.

Review disposition: accepted the leakage and interval critiques by removing June first-print outcome evidence and recomputing the point and interval from pre-release Jan-May data only; accepted the resolver critique by keeping the BLS official source while noting the ledger's ALFRED first-print adapter inconsistency.
